answer: In scope, with a base-CRM (not extension) modelling. Treat 'fire-keeper' as an E74 Group in the CRM's 'official position' sense: E74's own scope note explicitly covers 'official positions which used to be regarded ... as one actor, independent of the current holder of the office, such as the president of a country', adding 'it may happen that the group never had more than one member' -- exactly the fire-keeper post. Each succession is then an E85 Joining (P143 joined = the incoming fire-keeper, P144 joined with = the fire-keeper office) paired with an E86 Leaving for the outgoing fire-keeper (P145 separated / P146 separated from the same office); P107 has current or former member is the available shortcut if the full path is overkill. The informality is not a blocker: E85/E86 are E7 Activities, so each gets its own E52 Time-Span via P4 has time-span, and CRM's fuzzy-boundary primitives (P81a/b, P82a/b) are built precisely for 'somewhere in this multi-year window, no exact date' -- the mailing list shows this same pattern used for an informally-dated 18th-century club election (thread t0873). No ceremony, document, or witness is required by the model: the CIDOC CRM's own objectives note counts oral tradition as valid evidence, and CRM property quantifiers are optional so as to accommodate incomplete information. I did not reach for an extension (CRMaaa/SDHSS Social Role/Status classes), which the SIG itself points to for richer 'position within an institution' modelling (thread t1806, a 2024 case about a king's butler) -- but that thread also confirms CRMbase already has the two events needed here, just not a slicker way to bind the office-type to the Group's internal structure, which this case doesn't need.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: E8's scope note restricts it to transfers of legal ownership and says explicitly 'it does not, however, imply changes of any other kinds of rights' -- a customary, non-legal right to light the fire first does not fit.

rejected_alternatives.option: E30 Right / P105 right held by
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E30 can tag the privilege itself, but CRMbase has no modelled 'transfer of a Right' event distinct from E8 (which is ownership-only); the SIG's own 2024 thread on an analogous single-office case (t1806) says CRMbase 'does not offer other constructs' for this and points to extensions (CRMaaa/SDHSS) outside the family models this tool indexes, so I left it out rather than invent a shortcut.

Proposed in 2008 (thread t0426) but met a formal negative vote arguing the office-as-singleton-Group reading (thread t0431) makes it redundant, and it does not appear in the current v7.3.2 property list via docs search -- not safe to cite as a standing construct.

docs "uncertain fuzzy date of an event" --kind narrative
docs "Minimality principle do not model what cannot be documented" --kind narrative
notes: No thread argues this exact scenario (informal, unwitnessed office succession); the E74-as-office reading and the fuzzy-timespan precedent are each solid individually but I found no single episode where the SIG combined them for a case this informal, so I composed the answer from two separate lines of evidence rather than one on-point discussion.
